title: Portal Wall
subtitle: MIT Media Lab · 1985 → 2026
_note: Entries verified against the sources in each "source" field; images are freely licensed, see CREDITS.md. Optional per entry: depthScale (0..1, default 0.35), splat/splatFit/splatRotation/splatPosition/splatScale for a Gaussian splat memory.

entries.title: Put-That-There
entries.blurb: Richard Bolt's 'Put-That-There' paired speech recognition with pointing at a wall-sized display, so a pronoun and a gesture could move things around a map. The direct ancestor of what your hands are doing right now.
entries.credit: no freely licensed archive image found; typographic placeholder

entries.title: The Media Lab opens
entries.blurb: Nicholas Negroponte and Jerome Wiesner open the Lab in I.M. Pei's Wiesner Building, on the bet that computing, publishing and broadcast would converge.
entries.credit: John Phelan / Wiesner Building, MIT, Cambridge MA (2011) / CC BY 3.0

entries.title: Being Digital
entries.blurb: Bits, not atoms. Negroponte's 1995 book explained the Lab's worldview to everyone else and predicted an entirely digital society.
entries.credit: Gin Kai, U.S. Naval Academy, Photographic Studio / Nicholas Negroponte, Forrestal Lecture, US Naval Academy (2009) / CC BY-SA 3.0

entries.title: Things That Think
entries.blurb: The Things That Think consortium starts embedding sensing and computation into everyday objects and environments, years before anyone said 'Internet of Things'.
entries.credit: no freely licensed archive image found; typographic placeholder

entries.title: Affective Computing
entries.blurb: Rosalind Picard's book argues that machines must recognize, interpret and respond to human emotion. The field gets its name here.
entries.credit: Joi Ito / Faculty meeting at MIT Media Lab: Kent Larson, Deb Roy, Rosalind Picard (2014) / CC BY 2.0

entries.title: E Ink
entries.blurb: Joseph Jacobson's group and two MIT undergraduates spin out E Ink. Electrophoretic paper leaves the Lab and ends up in every e-reader.
entries.credit: htomari / E-ink display on Amazon Kindle 7th gen (2018) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: Tangible Bits
entries.blurb: Hiroshi Ishii and Brygg Ullmer's CHI 97 paper: grasp and manipulate digital information through physical objects and surfaces, coupling the worlds of bits and atoms.
entries.credit: jeanbaptisteparis / Hiroshi Ishii explains Topobo to Fumihiko Maki and Gary Kamemoto, MIT Media Lab (2010) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: LEGO Mindstorms RCX
entries.blurb: The programmable brick from Resnick's group, named for Papert's book, ships with LEGO as the Robotics Invention System: constructionism, boxed and sold.
entries.credit: Jean-Baptiste LABRUNE / LEGO Mindstorms RCX (2010) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: Center for Bits and Atoms
entries.blurb: Neil Gershenfeld's Center for Bits and Atoms launches on an NSF award. Its outreach fab labs seed a worldwide network of digital-fabrication workshops.
entries.credit: jeanbaptisteparis / Neil Gershenfeld (2010) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: Minority Report
entries.blurb: John Underkoffler, out of Ishii's Tangible Media Group, designs the film's gestural interface as its science adviser, then builds it for real as Oblong's g-speak. This wall is a nod to it.
entries.credit: Steve Jurvetson / John Underkoffler in the g-speak media matrix, TED 2010 / CC BY 2.0

entries.title: One Laptop per Child
entries.blurb: Announced at Davos in January and unveiled with Kofi Annan in Tunis that November: the $100 laptop. The XO-1 enters production in 2007.
entries.credit: World Economic Forum / Nicholas Negroponte presents the US$100 Laptop, World Economic Forum, Davos 2006 / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: Scratch
entries.blurb: Block programming for kids launches in May 2007. By 2023 more than 100 million users had shared over 120 million projects.
entries.credit: Wikimedia Commons contributor (screenshot); Scratch by MIT Media Lab / Scratch 3.0 editor screenshot (2023) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: Drawdio
entries.blurb: Jay Silver's pencil that draws music: a 555 timer, graphite and your own body close the circuit. Sold as a kit, it became a maker-movement classic.
entries.credit: Mike Lee / Two Adafruit Drawdio kits (2009) / CC BY 2.0

entries.title: SixthSense
entries.blurb: Pranav Mistry's pendant-sized projector and camera turn any surface into an interface. Shown at TED in February 2009, it became one of TED's most-watched demos.
entries.credit: Pranav Mistry / SixthSense framing-gesture camera, Pranav Mistry / Public domain

entries.title: Death and the Powers
entries.blurb: Tod Machover's robot opera, libretto by Robert Pinsky, premieres at the Opéra de Monte-Carlo in September 2010 and becomes a 2012 Pulitzer finalist.
entries.credit: Joi Ito / Tod Machover (2007) / CC BY 2.5

entries.title: E14 opens
entries.blurb: Fumihiko Maki's glass-and-steel extension opens on March 5, 2010: six storeys of double-height labs built to make the work visible.
entries.credit: Sayamindu Dasgupta / MIT Media Lab building E14 (2011) / CC BY-SA 2.0

entries.title: inFORM
entries.blurb: A dynamic shape display: a grid of motorized pins rises and falls so remote hands can push objects across a table.
entries.credit: no freely licensed archive image found; typographic placeholder

entries.title: Silk Pavilion
entries.blurb: 6,500 silkworms finish a dome of machine-laid silk threads: Neri Oxman's group lets biology do the fabrication.
entries.credit: Neri Oxman / Silk Pavilion, silkworms at work (2013) / CC BY-SA 4.0

entries.title: Bionic ballet
entries.blurb: At TED 2014 Hugh Herr's group puts Boston Marathon survivor Adrianne Haslet-Davis back on the dance floor, on a prosthesis built in 200 days.
entries.credit: Steve Jurvetson / The Debut of Bionic Ballet, TED 2014 / CC BY 2.0

entries.title: Space Exploration Initiative
entries.blurb: Ariel Ekblaw founds the Initiative in May 2016. Its first zero-g research flight follows in November 2017, then suborbital rockets and payloads to the ISS.
entries.credit: NASA/Jack Pfaller / Zero Gravity Corp. Boeing 727, the aircraft type used for the Lab's parabolic flights (KSC, 2007; not a Lab flight) / public domain

entries.title: AlterEgo
entries.blurb: Electrodes along the jaw read silent speech and bone conduction whispers the answer back: Arnav Kapur's wearable lets you talk to a machine without a sound.
entries.credit: no freely licensed archive image found; typographic placeholder

entries.title: 40 Years
entries.blurb: Founded in 1985, the Lab opened its fortieth year with an alumni reunion in October 2025 and marks the anniversary itself on October 21-24, 2026. Four decades of demos. This wall is one more.
entries.credit: ajay_suresh / MIT Media Lab, Building E14 (November 2025) / CC BY 4.0
